Cc: netops@acme.com
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: on-prem VPC circuitry walkthrough

Hi Soojin,

We're finalizing the network handoff for the on-prem deployment in our Boston colo and we'd like a focused walkthrough of the control-plane / data-plane demarcation and the physical circuit mapping. A few specifics we'd like covered:

- Where KV-cache traffic is expected to egress (IP ranges + NAT behavior)
- Boundary devices that sit between tenant VMs and the Redwood runtime (L2/L3 demarc)
- Failover behavior when the primary control-plane link degrades

We have the site circuit drawing attached (rough PDF) and can share traceroute outputs in advance if that helps. Are you available for a 45-minute session this week?

Thanks,
Jamie Park
Network Engineering
Acme Financial

Attachment: site-circuit-map-v1.pdf (diagram, 420KB)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>

Cc: netops@acme.com, jonas.weber@redwood.com, neha.kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request: on-prem VPC circuitry walkthrough

Hi Jamie — thanks for the PDF and the clear list. I'm available Thu 11/19 11:00–11:45 PT (14:00–14:45 ET) and can run a targeted walkthrough. Proposed agenda: 

1) Quick sync (5m): goals and success criteria (keep traffic local, avoid cross-tenant leakage, maintain <20ms control-plane p99)
2) Circuit map review (15m): review your site-circuit-map-v1.pdf and annotate where we expect control-plane vs data-plane egress
3) KV-cache & prefix caching (10m): expected IPs, NAT translation, and hints for local NAT sessions TTLs
4) Failover & SLOs (10m): link flapping, control-plane fallback to secondary, and how the runtime ramps down batches safely
5) Action items & artifacts (5m): runbook entries, required evidence for our ops cutover

Pre-reads that will speed the session: a short traceroute from the host facing the tenant VLAN and a basic NAT table dump (if allowed). I'll attach our current draft boundary diagram and a quick control/data flow SVG for reference.

I'll schedule the calendar invite and share a short agenda doc.

Thanks — looking forward to it.

Best,
So-ojin Lee
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0147

Attachments: kv-cache-boundary.png (stencil, 72KB); controlplane-dataflow.svg (vector, 24KB)

So — adding a few technical notes for the walkthrough and flagging risks we should be ready to show evidence for: 

- KV-cache egress: we recommend advertising a /29 from the colo provider as the NAT egress for the runtime cluster. If Acme wants to NAT at the tenant edge, we need an alignment doc.
- Control-plane keepalive: runtime sends 1s heartbeats; if round-trip times exceed 200ms for p95 we trigger a degraded-mode fallback where long-lived KV sessions are allowed to expire. Be ready to show p95 metrics for 72h pre-cutover.
- Link-degraded behavior: show staged rollback steps in the runbook — we should include a step to manually pin model variant to a lighter quantized profile before cutting traffic to a secondary path.

I'll attach an annotated SVG (controlplane-dataflow.svg) with callouts for where telemetry should be collected. Also — can we ask Acme for one sample NAT table and a packet capture of the initial handshake to make sure MTU/TCP MSS isn't causing fragmentation?

Cheers,
Jonas
Sr. Infrastructure Architect | Redwood Inference
